newsitem.title: USA: Rorer drug seen better than standard care.
newsitem.headline: Rorer drug seen better than standard care.

text.p: A study showed that Rhone-Poulenc Rorer Inc's anti-blood clot drug Lovenox worked better than the standard treatment in preventing death, heart attacks and angina in patients already suffering from a heart attack and severe chest pain, researchers said on Tuesday.

Data from a trial involving over 3,000 patients showed that after 14 days, 19.8 percent of those receiving the current standard of care, intravenous unfractionated heparin, either had a heart attack, recurring chest pain or died, researchers the Allegheny University of Health Sciences said.
Among those receiving Lovenox, 16.6 percent had a heart attack, chest pain or died, a 16 percent relative reduction, a statement from the university said.
Both groups also recieved aspirin, commonly used to avoid blood clots.
Lovenox is marketed by Rorer outside the U.S. under the tradename Clexane. It is a low-molecular-weight heparin and about one third the molecular size of standard heparin.
Rorer is majority ownd by French chemical group Rhone-Poulenc SA.
